To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully ported a weather and climate model to the FPGas, achieving 5.58 and 5.34 Gflop/s for single- and double-precision floating-point operations, respectively, on the Xilinx UltraScale + board.

the LFRic matrix-vector kernel has been implemented on a single Xilinx XCZU9E-2FFVB2104 FPGA and that the performance of the FPGA implementation of this kernel is 5.58 GFlops with single precision and 5,34 GFlops with double precision.

the LFRic matrix-vector kernel has been implemented on a Xilinx FPGA and that we have achieved 5.34 Gflop/s with a power consumption of 4.6 W and 5.57 Gflop/s at 4.7 W with double-precision floating-point arithmetic and 5.34 and 5.56 Gflop/s for single-precision floating-point, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the porting of scientific applications to the FPGA accelerators of the EuroExac architecture.
the porting of a high-performance scientific application to a new type of architecture, the EuroExa FPGA-based architecture.
porting the LFRice climate model to the EuroExa FPGA architecture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully ported the LFRic model to a single FPGA and have demonstrated a performance of 5 Gflops with double precision and of 5.6 Gflops with single precision.

the porting and implementation of a simple matrix-vector kernel from LFRic to a single FPGA on a development board has demonstrated the feasibility of using FPGAs for accelerating weather and climate models.
we are still in the early stages of the porting of LFRic to FPGAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LFRic kernel is a good candidate for FPGA acceleration and that the results we have obtained so far are promising.
the LFRic kernel has been implemented on the EuroExa FPGA accelerator and that the performance is competitive with the best published results.
the LFRic kernel has been successfully ported to the FPGA, and that we have demonstrated the feasibility of porting a HPC kernel to the FPGA.

it is possible to port a weather and climate model to the FPGas of the EuroExascale architecture.
, although the performance is not as high as might be expected, it is not too far from that which can be expected in the EuroExa context.
it is possible to port HPC applications to the FPGAS of the EuroExas architecture.
